title: Air-fryer beetroot
subtitle: Beetroot wedges roasted in the air fryer until tender and caramelised.
excerpt: Raw beetroot peeled and cut into wedges, air-fried until the cut faces caramelise and the inside is completely tender. Ready in 30 minutes. Serves four as a side.
sourceNotes: Beetroot is a root vegetable used throughout British cooking, most commonly roasted, pickled, or used raw in salads. The air fryer reduces the roasting time compared to a conventional oven and produces well-caramelised edges on the wedges.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast beetroot keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.

content.text: Raw beetroot is dense and takes longer than most vegetables in the air fryer. Cut into wedges rather than cubes so the flat faces caramelise while the thinner edge cooks through. Wear gloves when peeling and cutting ,  beetroot stains hands and surfaces deeply. The skin is edible but the texture improves significantly with peeling.

items.prepNote: medium, peeled and each cut into 6 wedges

content.text: Toss the {{beetroot}} wedges with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt until evenly coated. Preheat the air fryer to 190°C. Place in a single layer in the basket. Cook for 15 minutes, shake the basket, and cook for a further 12-15 minutes until the cut faces are caramelised and a skewer slides through without resistance. Drizzle with balsamic vinegar if using before serving.

items.symptom: Still hard in the centre after 30 minutes
items.cause: Beetroot cut too thick or were very large.
items.fix: Check by inserting a skewer ,  it should go through without resistance. If still firm, continue in 5-minute increments. Older, larger beetroot can take 40 minutes.

items.symptom: Edges burning before centre is cooked
items.cause: Temperature too high or wedges too thin.
items.fix: Cook at 190°C not 200°C. Cut into 6 wedges per beetroot, not 8 ,  thicker wedges cook through before the outside burns.
Beetroot loses some of its vivid red during roasting. The flavour concentrates and sweetens. The colour is not a sign of quality.

content.text: Air-fryer beetroot works as a side to roast lamb or duck, or tossed into a warm salad with goat's cheese, walnuts, and rocket. It is also good cold in a grain salad with farro or barley. The sweet-earthy flavour pairs well with something sharp ,  feta, pickled onion, or a citrus dressing.
